risk_note: RV2 (platform queue / logging / config, db migration). R-01 (D10-183 ②, D10-193): every business queue (15 on main, including union-auth and evt.notification-claim-result added since the first review) gets its own dead-letter queue <queue>.dead (order-sync.dead for the shared order-sync queue); a migration first creates the .dead queues in pgboss.queue (same settings as the old global dead-letter) and then repoints the existing queues' dead_letter (the foreign key is not deferrable), so a deployed database matches the new catalog and startup is not refused with queue_mismatch; release order is migrate first, then restart all processes. The entry plan still consumes no dead-letter queue (validation unchanged); a worker scheduled job counts jobs in each .dead queue by SQL (order-sync.dead grouped by data.platform) and logs one structured error per non-empty queue, never consuming, changing or replaying them; metrics export and alert rules follow in B1-01zzh. The root pino logger carries the deploy version from a new config item (staging passes COULI_API_TAG into the containers) and omits the field when unset. The schema snapshot is unchanged (the migration only writes pgboss.queue rows). Frozen tests that listed the global dead-letter target change only that expectation (ledger test_paths; class 1, label checked by the orchestrator under approvals #24); [AC-F1-09p#27] is declared red_exempt (body unchanged). No money, no attribution. After rebasing on 10-24, orchestrator mechanical test(spec) commits add the two newer queues to the rule-test queue list, change only the dead-letter expectation of their frozen catalog tests (test/spec/union/auth-probe/queue.test.ts, test/spec/notification/claim-result-message/routing.test.ts; ledger #1443) and create union-auth exclusive in the old-catalog replay fixture.
